newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines-Jan 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines-Jan 8.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- MING PAO -- Chief Executive-designate Tung Chee-hwa has reached an agreement with the Chinese team of the Joint Liaison Group over their different responsibilities and on ways of cooperation.

-- China's State Planning Commission said the nation was to increase its foreign borrowing to US$16 billion this year. It admitted that China was facing huge pressure for repayments on existing foreign loans.
-- TA KUNG PAO -- Chinese vice-Premier Qian Qichen said the situation in Hong Kong was encouraging and the sucess of "one country two systems" would cast a positive impact on the reunification.
-- Soldiers of the People's Liberation Army's Hong Kong Garrison were actively learning the law governing the garrison, and were determined to establish a civilised image in Hong Kong.

-- HONG KONG DAILY NEWS -- Tung Chee-hwa finally selected an office near in the Asia Pacific Finance Tower in Central to be his base until the handover. Fengshui experts said the new office's fengshui was better than that of Government House.
-- HONG KONG ECONOMIC JOURNAL -- Sources said Singapore Telecom might join hands with a mainland Chinese group to buy into Hongkong Telecom, but Singapore Telecom denied the story.

-- EXPRESS NEWS -- Former British foreign secretary Lord Howe said whole world was looking at Hong Kong's handover, and said it would be dangerous for the Hong Kong media to play up unexpected events during the handover period instead of the handover itself.
-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- A U.S. judge refused to send alleged cigarette smuggler Jerry Lui back to Hong Kong to face trial under the post-handover Special Administrative Region.
-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- Analysts said Cheung Kong (Holdings) might be poised for a major acquisition following the shake-up in the group and the takeover bid for Hongkong Electric.
